papers.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.
papers.overview_sentence: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people.

papers.title: FlippingAGR: A Flipping Aerial-Ground Robot With Dual-Mode Terrestrial Locomotion
papers.abstract: Combining aerial flight and ground mobility into a single platform, aerial-ground robots exhibit tremendous potential for performing complex tasks. However, existing designs predominantly adopt a fixed horizontal posture for ground locomotion, failing to fully exploit the potential of variable postures in traversing complex environments. To overcome this limitation, we presentFlippingAGR, a compactFlipping Aerial-GroundRobot that integrates a pair of flipping tracks, a thrust-vectoring mechanism, and a quadrotor propulsion system. Beyond flying capability, the robot supports two distinct terrestrial locomotion modes: crawling and balancing. In crawling mode, the robot actively positions the flipping tracks to achieve robust traversal over rough terrains. By actively deflecting the thrust direction via a thrust-vectoring mechanism to provide the driving force required for attitude balancing, and coordinating with the flipping tracks, the robot develops a novel variable-posture balancing locomotion mode, enabling it to traverse narrow spaces. Systematic dynamic modeling and analysis are conducted for each locomotion mode and the associated transition processes, and dedicated controllers are developed to ensure stable operation and smooth transition across all modes. Experimental results in indoor and outdoor environments show that the robot exhibits excellent traversability through low passages, rough terrain, and tilted narrow gaps.
papers.overview_sentence: Combining aerial flight and ground mobility into a single platform, aerial-ground robots exhibit tremendous potential for performing complex tasks.

papers.title: LA-WBC: Learning-Driven Adaptation of Whole-Body Control for Safe Locomotion on Uncertain Terrain
papers.abstract: This paper proposes Learning-driven Adaptation of Whole-Body Control (LA-WBC) for quadrupedal locomotion on terrains with uncertain friction. LA-WBC infers terrain friction from proprioceptive feedback and WBC command–response features, and jointly adapts the friction coefficient used in the contact constraints and the commanded locomotion velocity. Unlike end-to-end reinforcement learning (RL), the proposed framework retains the nominal WBC structure and remains compatible with established WBC safety and stability analyses. Hardware-informed model matching and feature scaling improve sim-to-real friction inference and prediction consistency. Compared with the evaluated RL baseline, the proposed pipeline requires approximately$\mathbf{12\%}$of the total data-generation and training time. Simulation and hardware experiments demonstrate improved velocity tracking, reduced foot slippage and base-motion variation, and higher locomotion success rates relative to non-adaptive WBC.
papers.overview_sentence: This paper proposes Learning-driven Adaptation of Whole-Body Control (LA-WBC) for quadrupedal locomotion on terrains with uncertain friction.

repos.readme_excerpt: Z-Mobile-Manip Supervised mobile manipulation for a Unitree Go2-W EDU quadruped carrying an AgileX PiPER 6-DoF arm and a wrist-mounted Intel RealSense D435. What this is The near-field half of a three-repository stack: navigation drives the robot to a coarse standoff, and this system takes over from about a metre out and runs through to a completed grasp and return. An RTX 4090 workstation does perception, grasp synthesis, IK, planning and the operator UI; the robot's onboard NUC owns the D435, PiPER can0 , joint feedback and the Go2-W WebRTC base transport, joined over ROS_DOMAIN_ID=20 . Open-vocabulary text is grounded with YOLOE , tracked with EdgeTAM , and back-projected against Fast-FoundationStereo depth rather than the D435's raw stream. Grasps come from AnyGrasp with a local antipodal generator as fallback, are solved by a damped Gauss-Newton Pinocchio IK, and are checked against a capsule model of the platform's own fixtures ( configs/piper_collision_capsules.json — the only enforced representation of the chassis, NUC and Mid-360 LiDAR) plus an observed point cloud. repos.readme_excerpt: Whole-Body Humanoid MPC This repository contains a Whole-Body Nonlinear Model Predictive Controller (NMPC) for humanoid loco-manipulation control. This approach enables to directly optimize through the full-order torque-level dynamics in realtime to generate a wide range of humanoid behaviors building up on an extended & updated version of ocs2 Interactive Velocity and Base Height Control via Joystick: It contains the following hardware platform agnostic MPC fromulations: Centroidal Dynamics MPC The centroidal MPC optimizes over the whole-body kinematics and the center off mass dynamics, with a choice to either use a single rigid body model or the full centroidal dynamics. This specific approach builds up on the centroidal model in ocs2 by generalizing costs and constraints to a 6 DoF contact among others. I am still working on documenting this.
